steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Polyrhythm (multiple conflicting rhythmic patterns simultaneously) is central to African music — it creates complex, layered rhythmic textures. | Key Fact: Caribbean genres each have distinct rhythmic signatures: reggae (off-beat skank guitar, one-drop drumming), ska (fast off-beat), calypso (syncopated melody). | Key Fact: Cyclic structures repeat musical patterns — unlike Western through-composed forms, African music often builds intensity through cyclical repetition and layering. | Key Fact: Afrobeat (Fela Kuti) combines West African highlife with jazz, funk and Yoruba music — it demonstrates how fusion creates entirely new genres.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe how african and caribbean fusion music are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use african and caribbean fusion music. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use african and caribbean fusion music in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.
